meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'The capitalists will sell us the rope with which we will hang them'?
meta.ogDescription: No match in Lenin's writings. The line first surfaces in 1955 American print, credited to Lenin with no source. Stalin and Marx credits are unsupported too.

answer.label: Not Vladimir Lenin — an unsourced Cold War attribution
answer.authorDates: First credited to Lenin in print in 1955, with no source given
answer.sourceLine: Researchers have found no match in Lenin’s writings. The earliest strong match located by Quote Investigator ↗ is a 1955 filler item in The Commonwealth, where Major George Racey Jordan claimed “Lenin wrote” that capitalists would “vie with each other for the rope contract.” Jordan gave no documentary source, and QI calls the evidence linking the line to Lenin weak.

source.excerpt: Lenin wrote, “When it comes time to hang the capitalists, they will vie with each other for the rope contract.” —Major George Racey Jordan
trail: 1920 — Lenin’s real rope line, in chapter 9 of “Left-Wing” Communism: he would support Henderson “in the same way as the rope supports a hanged man.” Capitalists and selling are not mentioned. Marxists Internet Archive ↗
1955 — The earliest strong match located by Quote Investigator: a filler in The Commonwealth crediting Lenin through Major George Racey Jordan, with no documentary source. Quote Investigator ↗
1959 — Congressman Walter H. Judd tells a House committee that Lenin said the capitalists “will bid against each other for the sale of the rope.” Quote Investigator ↗
Today — Wikiquote lists “We will hang the capitalists with the rope that they sell us” under Lenin’s Misattributed section. Wikiquote ↗
source.excerptNote: This is the wording as Quote Investigator transcribes it from the 1955 filler. The familiar form, “The capitalists will sell us the rope with which we will hang them,” is a later variant. Neither form has been found in anything Lenin wrote.

source.rightsNote: The popular wording has no identifiable author or first publication, so no rights status is claimed for it. Lenin’s genuine 1920 rope passage is quoted here from Julius Katzer’s English translation in the Progress Publishers Collected Works, vol. 31 (1964), a post-1931 translation, as listed by the Marxists Internet Archive ↗.

author.name: Vladimir Lenin
author.kicker: The man it is pinned on
author.heading: About Vladimir Lenin
author.metaLine: 1870–1924 · Russian revolutionary, founding head of Soviet Russia and the USSR
author.bio: Vladimir Ilyich Lenin led the Bolshevik Revolution and was the first head of government of Soviet Russia (1917–1924) and of the Soviet Union (1922–1924). He left a very large body of published work, and the rope saying appears nowhere in it. His own best-known rope image, from “Left-Wing” Communism: An Infantile Disorder (1920), is about backing British Labour leaders “in the same way as the rope supports a hanged man.” It is not about capitalists selling anything.

misattribution.heading: Who gets the credit, and why it fails
misattribution.intro: Quote Investigator notes that this saying about short-sighted greed has been pinned on three famous communists. None of the three credits holds up.

items.why: Multiple researchers have found no match in Lenin’s writings. The first strong match that Quote Investigator ↗ could find dates from 1955, “many years after Lenin’s death in 1924,” and that item names no documentary source.
Senator Barry Goldwater credited Stalin in his 1979 memoir With No Apologies. Quote Investigator ↗ finds no substantive evidence for this.
In 2007 an investment fund manager credited “Karl Marx and Vladimir Lenin” in testimony to a U.S. Senate committee. Quote Investigator ↗ finds no substantive evidence for Marx.

Wikiquote suggests the saying may be a confused paraphrase of chapter 9 of “Left-Wing” Communism ↗. There Lenin backs Henderson “as the rope supports a hanged man.” Nobody sells anything in that passage, and it is about British Labour politicians, not capitalists.

In a 1975 Washington speech, Solzhenitsyn told a story in which Karl Radek asks where the rope will come from and Lenin answers, “They’ll supply us with it.” Quote Investigator ↗ says it does not know where Solzhenitsyn got the story.

misattribution.truthLine: The line’s true originator is unknown. It first appears in American print in 1955, already credited to Lenin and with no source, and it has not been found in his works. The closest match in meaning that Quote Investigator ↗ found is a 1931 profile of Maxim Litvinov, which says millionaires who funded a 1905 Bolshevik newspaper “helped weave the rope from which many of them should hang later on.”

context.heading: Why it caught on
lead: The saying spread during Cold War arguments about trade with the Soviet bloc. It turned an abstract worry, that Western firms would sell the Soviets what they needed to win, into a joke that sticks. Quote Investigator traces it through a 1959 syndicated column by Victor Riesel, where a Soviet diplomat supposedly recalled that capitalists would “outbid each other for the sale of the hemp.” Two weeks later Congressman Walter H. Judd repeated it before a House committee.

The nearest documented idea is a passage reported by I. U. Annenkov in a 1961 Novyi Zhurnal article, “Remembrances of Lenin.” Annenkov said capitalists would furnish credits and materials and “work on the preparation of their own suicide.” Quote Investigator notes it matches the meaning but uses no rope metaphor, and it comes from a memoir published decades after the fact, not from Lenin’s published works.
context.pull: Lenin’s real rope supported a hanged man. It was never for sale.

sourcesVerified.claim: Earliest strong match QI located is a 1955 filler in The Commonwealth (Oct 31, 1955, vol. 31 no. 44, p. 268) crediting Lenin via Major George Racey Jordan with the 'vie with each other for the rope contract' wording; no documentary source; researchers cannot find it in Lenin's writings

QI conclusion: evidence linking the saying to Lenin is weak because the first citation appeared in 1955, many years after Lenin's death in 1924; no substantive evidence for Stalin or Marx; the 1931 Litvinov citation matches the meaning; QI does not know how Solzhenitsyn acquired the anecdote

Judd 1959 House committee 'bid against each other for the sale of the rope'; Riesel 1959 column 'outbid each other for the sale of the hemp'; Goldwater 1979 With No Apologies credits Stalin; 2007 Senate testimony credits Marx and Lenin; Solzhenitsyn 1975 Radek anecdote; Annenkov 1961 Novyi Zhurnal credits passage
